title: Regular coordinate intersections and their etale transport
statement: Let $U$ be a regular locally Noetherian scheme [def-weil-regular-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth], let $s\geq1$, and let $t_1,\ldots,t_s\in\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$. Assume that at each $u\in U$ the germs with indices $I(u)=\{j:t_j(u)=0\text{ in }\kappa(u)\}$ are members at distinct positions of a regular system of parameters of $\mathcal O_{U,u}$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters]. For every $J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,s\}$ define the closed subscheme $C_J=V(t_j:j\in J)$ [def-weil-closed-immersion], with $C_{\varnothing}=U$. Every $C_J$ is locally Noetherian, regular and reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme], and may be empty. For $u\in C_J$ its local ring is $\mathcal O_{C_J,u}=\mathcal O_{U,u}/(t_j:j\in J)$, a regular local integral domain. Let $e:W\to U$ be any etale morphism [def-weil-etale-morphism], and write $t'_j=e^*t_j$. Then $W$ is regular and locally Noetherian. For each $w\in W$, $u=e(w)$, the local map $\mathcal O_{U,u}\to\mathcal O_{W,w}$ carries every regular system of parameters to a regular system of parameters, and $t'_j(w)=0$ in $\kappa(w)$ if and only if $t_j(u)=0$ in $\kappa(u)$. In particular the vanishing pulled-back germs again occupy distinct positions in a regular system of parameters. Scheme-theoretically $C_J\times_U W=V(t'_j:j\in J)$, and all these pulled-back intersections are locally Noetherian, regular and reduced, including the empty cases.

proof.text: For the coordinate closed immersion i, the proved source-library theorem Scheme.Hom.ker_stalkMap computes its stalk kernel on an affine neighborhood. The ofIdealTop_ideal and Ideal.map_span equations, followed by germ_res_apply, identify this kernel with the span of the chosen global coordinate germs. The closed-immersion stalk map is surjective, so RingHom.quotientKerEquivOfSurjective gives the canonical quotient equivalence with the required formula. Local finite type and local Noetherianity of the closed subscheme are existing Mathlib instances. This packages the affine localization and quotient calculation of the original plan without repeating it.

source.place: Tag 00CT (proposition-localize-quotient); schemes.tex Tag 01HV (lemma-spec-sheaves), part (6); morphisms.tex Tag 01T6 (lemma-finite-type-noetherian)

proof.text: At $u\in C_J$ every $t_{j,u}$ with $j\in J$ belongs to the maximal ideal, so $J\subseteq I(u)$. By hypothesis these germs occupy distinct positions in a full regular parameter system of the regular local ring $A=\mathcal O_{U,u}$. Permute that system to put the $|J|$ selected positions first; a permutation still has length $\dim A$ and generates the same maximal ideal. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence] with $c=|J|$ to see that the quotient computed in Step 1 is regular local. By [lem-sc-regular-local-domain] it is an integral domain, hence has no nonzero nilpotents: if $b^n=0$, repeated cancellation in a domain gives $b=0$. The locally Noetherian stalk criterion in [def-weil-regular-scheme] now makes $C_J$ regular, and [def-pc-reduced-scheme] makes it reduced. When $J=\varnothing$ use $c=0$; when $C_J=\varnothing$ the assertions about its points are vacuous.

proof.text: An etale morphism is locally of finite type by the existing Mathlib instances (through smoothness and local finite presentation). Apply LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian to the locally Noetherian target. The existing Noetherian-stalk instance supplies Noetherianity at every source point; no quasi-compactness is used.

proof.text: At w choose affine source and target neighborhoods for the etale map. IsAffineOpen.arrowStalkMapIso identifies the stalk map with the localized affine ring map. Apply lem-sc-etale-local-dimension and transport dimensions across the two ring equivalences. The proved source-library FormallyUnramified.map_maximalIdeal_stalkMap identifies the extended maximal ideal with the source maximal ideal. Ideal.map_span and List.mem_map transport the generating equality of any regular parameter list, and List.length_map with dimension equality transports its length condition. Source regularity follows from the proved isRegularLocalRing_stalk_of_etale theorem. This handles empty parameter lists as well.

source.place: Tag 07QP (lemma-dimension-etale-extension), and the parameter-generator argument in Tag 0AH0 (lemma-regular-etale-extension); algebra.tex Tag 00U4 (lemma-etale-at-prime)

proof.text: By [def-weil-residue-field], the stalk map induces a homomorphism of fields $\kappa(u)\to\kappa(w)$, carrying the residue of $t_j$ to that of $t'_j$. Such a homomorphism is injective: if a nonzero element $a$ mapped to zero then $1=aa^{-1}$ would map to zero. Consequently $t'_j(w)=0$ if and only if $t_j(u)=0$, so $I(w)=I(u)$ as indexed subsets. Transport a parameter system containing those marked positions using Step 4. The same positions give the vanishing pulled-back germs; distinct positions remain distinct positions of that list.

source.place: Tag 00U4 (lemma-etale-at-prime), residue-field clause; elementary injectivity of a homomorphism of fields

proof.text: The proved source-library Scheme.IdealSheafData.comap_ofIdealTop theorem identifies the pullback of an ideal generated by global sections with the ideal generated by their images. Ideal.map_span and Set.image_image identify those images with the pulled-back coordinate functions. Compose pullbackSymmetry with IdealSheafData.comapIso and the ideal-equality isomorphism to obtain the required isomorphism over W. Use the parameter transport and residue-field vanishing equivalence from Steps 4-5 to repeat the coordinate quotient/regularity argument of Steps 1-2 on W. No nonemptiness is needed.
